userStories.title: The drift guard — hand-edit detection + --check
userStories.description: Two layers, both CI-runnable without the sibling repo: (1) a pytest that, for EACH generated seed (platform-management-skill.md, platform-operations-skill.md), recomputes the body sha and asserts it matches the sha recorded in the file's own banner — a hand-edit to a seed (the 'never edit live in the platform' violation) breaks the match and fails CI with a message pointing at automatos-skills + the sync script. (2) the same pytest invokes sync-auto-skill.py --check IF ../automatos-skills exists (developer machines) and SKIPS that half cleanly in CI with an explicit reason — the sha layer is the always-on guard, the --check layer is the freshness guard where the sibling is present.

userStories.title: [MEDIUM] platform-operations L1 trigger (Skill.description) never refreshes after the first seed — the 'single source, no drift' claim is false for the trigger text
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (both reviewers, CONFIRMED). PRD-231 makes the L1 trigger LOAD-BEARING: platform-operations renders as one L1 catalog line whose text is Skill.description (SkillsSection._l1_metadata_line), and that is Auto's only cue to call platform_load_skill. But that description is only ever set on the CREATE path: seed_auto_agent.py:423-435 resolves resolved_description from the seed frontmatter, and _upsert_builtin_core_skill returns early (:399-401) whenever the global builtin-core row already exists. The single mechanism this PRD wires to propagate seed edits to existing rows — skill_loader._refresh_builtin_if_stale (:939-974, per its own comment at :930-933) — updates prompt_template + content_hash ONLY, never skill.description. WORSE: its staleness trigger is a sha over the BODY (:959-962 early-returns when body hash matches), and a frontmatter-description-only edit changes neither the body nor the banner sha, so the refresh does not even fire. Failure scenario: US-006 telemetry shows the ops trigger under-fires (PRD §7's named risk); a maintainer edits the frontmatter description in automatos-skills to bite harder and runs sync-auto-skill.py; the seed file updates but the LIVE global Skill.description — the actual rendered L1 trigger — stays frozen at the first-seeded value. The tuning silently no-ops; the only remedy is a manual DB UPDATE. The comment 'the AUTHORED frontmatter description (single source — no hardcoded drift)' at seed_auto_agent.py:423-425 is falsified.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — _refresh_builtin_if_stale (skill_loader.py) now parses the frontmatter description and treats description drift as staleness on its OWN axis: body_stale = content_hash!=disk_hash; desc_stale = frontmatter desc present AND the row's existing non-empty description differs. The body-hash early-return no longer short-circuits a trigger-only edit — when only the description moved, the refresh fires and updates just skill.description.
